units.P1: excluded: summary lead of the release commands; its commitments are owned by the children build.test, build.test-output, build.package, build.verify, build.publish and build.makedeployed (packaging-deployed-code page)

build.reason: Pure heading for the release commands. Every command it names is owned by a child block (build.test, build.test-output, build.package, build.verify, build.publish here; build.makedeployed on the packaging-deployed-code page). No additional obligation.

obligations.text: `test <module>` runs the module's Phase="test" unit-test resource in the current namespace; a Phase="verify" resource is not run.
obligations.cases: test command with a test-phase and a verify-phase UnitTest resource sharing one directory

obligations.text: Test-scoped resources are loaded and compiled only by a command whose phase list contains their scope phase (test for Scope=test); other commands leave them out.
obligations.cases: scoped vs unscoped resource; command phase list with vs without the scope phase (test vs verify vs load)
obligations.observation: resource loaded/compiled after the phase walk

obligations.text: Test-scoped dependencies load for the test phase only.
A module's test classes are loaded at load time only in developer mode.
obligations.cases: load with dev vs without dev

obligations.text: The test phase loads every class under the test resource's directory (including other resources' packages), then compiles and runs the resource's own package.
obligations.cases: test phase on a directory holding the test and verify packages
obligations.observation: both packages defined; only the test package compiled and run

obligations.text: As built (C:D48), the test phase never deletes the test classes it loaded, even for a non-developer module; they stay (including verify-only packages that did not run) until uninstall.
obligations.cases: non-dev load then test then uninstall; dev load then test then uninstall
obligations.observation: test/verify classes defined after test and after uninstall

units.B5: excluded: observation-scope statement (status and report-file existence are separate observations; a reporting check does not prove verify cleanup)

obligations.text: `test` and `verify` print a summary of results.
obligations.cases: test vs verify; any outcome
obligations.gap: readers.rs json_device sets summary=true only for the JSON device output of the test phase. The plain-text default summary (Test/Abstract GetSummary through OutputToDevice without -format) and the verify command's summary in the VERIFY namespace are not modeled, so no rule contrasts a run that prints a summary with one that does not.

obligations.text: -quiet shows only the summary and failures; -verbose adds per-method results when used with -format.
obligations.cases: default vs -quiet vs -verbose (with -format)
obligations.observation: which sections the device output contains
obligations.gap: json_device(show_detail, verbose) distinguishes summary-only, failures and all-methods sections (control quiet-device-includes-all rejected), but show_detail/verbose are inputs: the mapping from the -quiet, -verbose and -format flags (Lifecycle/Base.cls %Test into Test/JsonOutput OutputToDevice) is not modeled, and only the JSON device is covered (YAML, TOON and plain-text device output are not).

obligations.text: -format json|yaml|toon, or the TestReportFormat setting, selects the summary format.
obligations.cases: -format given vs only TestReportFormat set vs neither; each format value
obligations.gap: No model selects the summary renderer. iter41 settings.rs and playbook settings.rs only validate and store TestReportFormat. Contrast to close: TestReportFormat=yaml with no -format prints YAML; -format json with TestReportFormat=yaml prints JSON (precedence); neither prints the default text summary.

obligations.text: -output-file writes the full results; the file extension picks the format (.json, .yaml, .toon, or .xml for JUnit).
obligations.cases: extension .json vs .yaml vs .toon vs .xml vs unsupported
obligations.gap: report_result takes extension_supported as an input Boolean and json_file fixes the JSON file contract to the full tree. The extension-to-format dispatch (.yaml -> YamlOutput, .xml -> JUnit) is not modeled, so no rule contrasts .yaml producing YAML with .xml producing JUnit, or an unsupported extension (.csv) refusing.

obligations.text: The output-file export happens before summary rendering: an unsupported summary format returns an error after valid results were written; the same passing tests with a supported summary format return success.
obligations.cases: unsupported vs supported summary format with a requested, supported output file

obligations.text: All formats print the same method and assertion counts.
obligations.cases: JSON vs YAML vs TOON summaries for one result tree
obligations.gap: summary_json/summary_yaml/summary_toon are each the identity on one shared Summary, so summaries_agree holds by definition. No model renders each format's counts from the tree (Test/JsonOutput, YamlOutput, ToonOutput summary paths), so a renderer that miscounts could not be distinguished.

obligations.text: JSON keeps assertion and error text exactly; as built (C:D53) YAML and TOON drop carriage returns, and YAML reads back with a trailing newline and without the first line's leading spaces.
obligations.cases: messages with punctuation, LF, CRLF and leading spaces in each format
obligations.observation: text read back from the report file

obligations.text: TOON writes one row per assertion; a method with an error and no assertions gets an error row and a status row.
obligations.cases: method with 2 assertions vs method with an error and 0 assertions

obligations.text: `package <module>` exports the module and bundles it into a .tgz archive.
obligations.cases: successful vs failing export
obligations.gap: scope.rs archive() adds the manifest to the copied UnitTest path map; ordinary resource export, the tar/gzip bundling and export failure are premises. No rule contrasts a successful export that yields the archive with a failing export (Lifecycle/Base.cls %Export error) that leaves none.

obligations.text: A deployed-item helper has a known error-propagation gap during package export.
-path sets where the archive goes, and only the archive is left there.
obligations.cases: package with -path vs default
obligations.observation: files left in the target directory
obligations.gap: No model of Lifecycle/Base.cls %Package output-directory handling. Contrast: package -path /tmp/x leaves exactly <module>-<version>.tgz in /tmp/x with the staging export removed, versus the default location.

obligations.text: -export-deps controls whether dependencies are included, and -export-python-deps adds Python dependencies.
obligations.cases: -export-deps 1 vs 0; -export-python-deps on vs off
obligations.observation: dependency modules and wheels inside the archive
obligations.gap: No model of the dependency/Python export branches of %Package/%Export. Contrast: a module with one dependency packaged with -export-deps 1 contains the dependency's archive, with 0 it does not; -export-python-deps adds the requirements' wheels.

obligations.text: Test-scoped resources are left out of the package unless their phase is requested or test inclusion adds it; -include-tests enables inclusion; an explicit -DIncludeTests=0 overrides a true <IncludeTests>.
obligations.cases: flag vs manifest vs explicit zero vs none; test-scoped vs unscoped resource
obligations.basis: reused:scopes.rs (project map %Export) and iter10 scope.rs (build.package.test-path metadata)

obligations.text: A UnitTest resource's Phase sets its returned child scope; export requires both the declared Scope and that returned scope to match the requested phases, and a matching test directory is copied with its file contents.
obligations.cases: declared Scope verify with Phase test under phases [test], [verify], [test,verify]; file under the directory vs sibling prefix

obligations.text: Test inclusion adds Test and Verify to the export phases; an explicit IncludeTests, including zero, overrides the manifest for that addition.
An explicit IncludeTests=0 does not remove a phase already requested.
obligations.cases: export phases already containing Test with IncludeTests=0 vs without
obligations.gap: export_phases returns the base list unchanged when inclusion is off, but every theorem and neighbour uses base [Package]. No rule exercises a base list already containing Test with param Some(false), so a variant that strips Test on zero would still verify.

obligations.text: Direct child enumeration does not return the test directory; export adds it after the scope checks. Archives omit it by default, include it by flag or manifest, and omit it again under the explicit zero override.
obligations.cases: none vs -include-tests vs manifest true vs explicit zero
obligations.observation: test file present in the archive

units.B2: excluded: pointer to the open policy question build.package.include-refresh.policy (undecided alternative)

obligations.text: Reloading an existing module with IncludeTests omitted keeps the stored value; an explicit false clears it; a command-only zero disables inclusion for that command and leaves the stored value unchanged.
obligations.cases: stored true + omitted vs explicit false; command override 0 vs none

obligations.text: A later package command with no override includes tests again when the stored value is still true.
obligations.cases: after a command-only zero, package with no override

obligations.text: A fresh module with IncludeTests omitted starts false.
obligations.cases: first load with the element omitted vs explicit true
obligations.gap: The initial stored value is an input (old=false, matrix_prior(0)=false). The fresh-module default from XML import of %IPM.Storage.Module (no prior record) is not modeled, so a default of true would still verify.

obligations.text: Working assumption: preserve the checked behavior (omission keeps, explicit false clears).
Extracting a named regular archive entry creates a file even when its size is zero.
obligations.cases: size 0 vs nonzero regular named entry

obligations.text: After a zero-size entry the next header is still read; an empty filename in the header, not a zero payload size, ends the archive.
obligations.cases: zero-size named entry vs empty-name header
obligations.observation: next header offset; end of archive

obligations.text: Directory copying refuses a target that is the source, contains it or lies inside it; a separate sibling directory is allowed.
obligations.cases: target == source, child, parent vs sibling

obligations.text: The overlap refusal happens before anything is deleted or copied.
obligations.cases: overlapping target with delete-first requested vs sibling
obligations.observation: source and target files after the refused call
obligations.gap: copy_ok is a Boolean with no filesystem state, so it cannot distinguish refusal-before-delete from delete-then-refuse. Contrast: Utils/File.cls::CopyDir(src, src/child, pDeleteFirst=1) leaves every nested source file intact (native S6-03 only).

obligations.text: A sibling target receives the nested files when the filesystem copy succeeds.
obligations.cases: sibling target, provider success vs failure
obligations.observation: nested files present in the target
obligations.gap: copy_ok(provider_ok) returns a Boolean; nested file contents are not represented, so no rule shows src/a/b.txt arriving at sibling/a/b.txt.

obligations.text: The Python check detects aliases (for example symlinks) through device and inode ancestry.
obligations.cases: aliased target whose real path is inside the source vs unaliased sibling
obligations.gap: same_inode_ancestor is an input; Utils/File.cls::DirectoriesOverlapPython's ancestry walk is not modeled, so the alias detection itself is a premise.

obligations.text: Without Python or file IDs, the fallback compares normalized directory paths, so an alias is not detected there.
obligations.cases: Python available vs unavailable on the same aliased target
obligations.gap: No model of the branch selection between DirectoriesOverlapPython and the path fallback; the alias flag is supplied by the caller. Contrast: the same symlinked target is refused with Python and allowed by the fallback.

obligations.text: `verify <module>` packages the module, installs the package into the VERIFY namespace with journaling off and runs its integration tests there.
obligations.cases: fresh VERIFY setup vs reuse/skip-load; passing vs failing integration test
obligations.observation: namespace created, NoJournal parameter, package installed, tests run
obligations.gap: verify_plan gives only the setup plan (create, load, NoJournal on a fresh create). Packaging, installing the package (not the source) into <ns>-VERIFY, running the Verify-phase tests there and the command outcome are not modeled; no contrast between a failing and a passing integration test.

obligations.text: With -only, the VERIFY namespace loads the module from its folder on disk instead of the package.
obligations.cases: verify vs verify -only
obligations.observation: source of the module loaded into VERIFY
obligations.gap: No model of the -only branch of Lifecycle/Base.cls %Verify. Contrast: with -only the VERIFY module root is the source folder; without, it is the extracted package.

obligations.text: `publish <module>` packages the module and sends it to a repository that allows publishing.
obligations.cases: publish-enabled vs non-publishing repository; package success vs failure
obligations.gap: publish_lifecycle takes package_ok and server_found as inputs, and capability() is not connected to repository choice. Selection of a publish-enabled repository (Repo/Manager over configured servers) is not modeled; contrast: two repositories, only one with publishing enabled, publish writes only there.

obligations.text: -repo picks the repository to publish to.
obligations.cases: -repo r1 vs -repo r2 vs default
obligations.gap: No model of Main.cls publish argument handling for -repo. Contrast: same module published with -repo a and -repo b lands in a and b respectively.

obligations.text: -use-external-name publishes under the external name.
`unpublish [<repo>/]<module> <version|all>` deletes a published package, asks first unless -force, and requires the registry to still allow deletion.
obligations.cases: confirm yes/no vs -force; registry allows vs refuses; version vs all
obligations.observation: remote package present after the command
obligations.gap: The registry permission and the all/version choice are modeled as Booleans, but the confirmation prompt and -force (Main.cls::Unpublish) are not. Contrast: without -force and answer no the package remains; with -force it is deleted.

obligations.text: `unpublish` fails when the module or version does not exist or the registry refuses.
obligations.cases: missing module/version vs registry refusal vs success
obligations.gap: Only the HTTP status contract (exactly 200) is modeled. The existence check for the module/version before deletion is not, so a nonexistent version reporting success could not be distinguished.

obligations.text: Publishing with -use-external-name makes the registry key the module's external name.
obligations.cases: use_external true vs false

obligations.text: It does not rename the module inside the archived manifest.
obligations.cases: use_external true
obligations.observation: module name in the archived manifest

obligations.text: Installing by the external registry key installs the original internal module name.
obligations.cases: install <external key>
obligations.gap: Only the archived name is modeled; the install reader (Utils/Module.cls::LoadModuleReference then Storage/Module.cls::NameExists) is not. Contrast: after install <external>, NameExists(internal) is true and NameExists(external) false.

obligations.text: The default publish mode uses the internal name for the key.
obligations.cases: use_external false

obligations.text: Empty or invalid chosen publish names are refused before publication.
obligations.cases: empty/invalid external name vs valid
obligations.gap: publish_lifecycle has a name_valid input, but the validation decision in Lifecycle/Base.cls %Publish is not modeled and no theorem exercises name_valid=false. Contrast: external name "" is refused with no remote write.

units.B3: excluded: evidence-scope statement (provider results are explicit inputs; multi-tag failure, cleanup errors and post-publication export were not exercised end to end)

obligations.text: A failed publish or unpublish does not establish that the registry is unchanged: as built, ORAS writes or deletes tags one at a time, so a later failure can follow completed earlier calls.
obligations.cases: first tag call succeeds, second fails, for push and delete
obligations.observation: registry tag map after the failure

obligations.text: ORAS cleanup can fail after the push succeeded, so the command fails with the package published.
obligations.cases: cleanup ok vs fails after a written push

obligations.text: The lifecycle can publish before its optional local version export fails; the in-memory version assignment does not show the stored row or manifest was updated.
obligations.cases: local export ok vs fails after a new version was published

obligations.text: Remote publishing and deletion require credentials and exactly HTTP 200 for success.
obligations.cases: status 200 vs 201/204; with vs without password

obligations.text: As built, ORAS permission probing reports deletion enabled before attempting the operation.
obligations.cases: any ORAS repository

obligations.text: An HTTP error or other returned error may follow external effects.
obligations.cases: provider wrote then returned an error
